claude.sample_unit: dermatology and dermatopathology professionals rating six fictitious reports
unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering with a structured custom GPT versus basic prompt for simplifying pathology reports for patients

links.outcome: Factualness, completeness, and harmfulness of simplified reports
links.effect: Mean factualness/completeness 1.27-1.63; harmfulness 1.31-1.83; DermDecoder significantly worse on some completeness and harmfulness outcomes.
links.quote: Mean ratings ranged from 1.27 to 1.63 (factualness/completeness) and 1.31-1.83 (harmfulness), indicating "Agree" to "Mostly Agree" or "Completely Harmless" to "Mostly Harmless."

unlisted_practices: Prompt-engineered custom GPT for simplifying dermatopathology reports for patients compared with a basic ChatGPT prompt

links.outcome: report factualness, completeness, and potential harm
links.effect: Prompt engineering showed no advantage; DermDecoder had worse completeness in psoriasis (p=0.007) and harmfulness in molluscum contagiosum (p=0.049) and melanoma in situ (p=0.048)
links.quote: Prompt engineering offered no advantage over basic AI usage in balancing professional accuracy with patient accessibility, necessitating human-in-the-loop oversight for AI-generated explanations.
